gaps.title: 10 validation rules have zero test coverage
gaps.description: Phase2OnlyNeedsConfigs, Phase2OnlyWrongMode, WarpPresetNotAllowed, WarpCidrsNotAllowed, InvalidPhase2Concurrency, ConfigEntryTooLong, SniTooLong, WgconfTooLong, TooManyEndpoints, and HTTP config entry rejection in phase2 are all validated in code but never exercised by any test. A regression removing any of these checks would go unnoticed.

gaps.title: Boundary values missing for concurrency, timeout, probes_per_endpoint, accepted_http_codes
gaps.description: concurrency: tested 0 reject and 1001 reject, but never 1 accept or 1000 accept. timeout_ms: tested 50 reject, but never 99 reject / 100 accept / 30000 accept / 30001 reject. probes_per_endpoint: tested 0 reject and 11 reject, but never 1 accept or 10 accept. accepted_http_codes: tested 99 reject and 600 reject, but never 100 accept or 599 accept. loss_threshold = 0 (valid) is untested. phase2 concurrency 0 and >8 are untested. f32::INFINITY for min_speed_mbps is untested (NaN and -1.0 are tested, but is_finite() also catches infinity).

gaps.title: ScanEvent::Phase2Progress and ScanEvent::Failed have no serde round-trip tests
gaps.description: The serde round-trip test for ScanEvent only covers Progress, Result, and Finished variants. Phase2Progress and Failed variants have zero round-trip coverage, meaning a serde attribute regression on either variant would go undetected.

gaps.title: Verdict round-trip only tests legacy defaults, not all fields
gaps.description: verdict_new_fields_default_when_absent only verifies that omitted fields default correctly. There is no round-trip test for a fully-populated Verdict with sent, received, loss_pct, fail_reason, asn, isp, and phase2 all set. A serde regression on any of these fields would be missed.

gaps.title: No serde round-trips for WarpConfig, full Phase2Config, or payload types
gaps.description: WarpConfig has no round-trip test at all. Phase2Config only tests probe_urls, not the full struct (configs, fragment, snis, concurrency, custom_fragment). ResultsPayload, StatusPayload, RangesPayload, ExportConfigRequest/Response, and RegisterRequest/Response have no round-trip coverage.

gaps.title: No invalid configs would incorrectly pass validation
gaps.description: All validation logic is correct — no invalid config can pass validate(). The risk is purely that the untested paths could regress silently. The code is sound; only the test coverage has gaps.

issues: No test for --json-errors flag behavior (defined as a contract in AGENTS.md)
No test for invalid --export-format value (e.g. --export-format xml)
No cleanup guard (Drop-style) on temp dirs — panics before remove_dir_all leak directories
live_tiny_scan has redundant gating (both #[ignore] and env-var return)
e2e_scan test assumes 203.0.113.0/30 is routable-per-policy without a comment explaining this assumption
Zero error-case tests — no coverage for bad URLs, timeouts, 404s, or malformed subscriptions
vless_fixture_dials_its_own_server connects to a hardcoded live Cloudflare Worker IP — fails silently if the Worker is redeployed or down
subscription test only checks specs.is_empty() and basic field presence — does not verify protocol, security, or WebSocket settings
assert!(... .expect(...)) pattern panics on fetch failure rather than testing graceful degradation
Both tests depend on live Cloudflare infrastructure making flakiness inherently high
No proptest for full wgconf round-trip — parse_wgconf (full config) is only covered deterministically, not fuzzed with random data
No property test for export output format validity
wg_ini_round_trips uses parse_wg_entry (INI-level) not parse_wgconf (full config level) — lower-level parser is fuzzed but higher-level is not
tunnel_probe_lifecycle has a conditional skip that silently passes if CF_SCANNER_DATA_DIR is not honored — test may pass without testing anything
fake_xray_child holds the socket for 120 seconds — if test hangs it blocks for 2 minutes before failing
No test for spawn failure modes (missing binary, dgst mismatch, port already in use)
ENV_LOCK with std::sync::Mutex in async code — safe in this case but the await_holding_lock suppression hides a potential maintenance hazard
FAKE_SRC parses config JSON by text splitting on 'port' — fragile if xray config format changes
rustc invocation only checks status.success() — no check of stderr for compilation errors
No test for write_fake_xray failure paths (e.g. rustc not on PATH)
No test for spawn failure modes (missing binary, dgst mismatch, port in use)

issues.title: Feature gating is correct and complete
issues.description: FakeTransport is gated cfg(any(test, feature="test-helpers")). FakeSub, FakeTunnelProbe, FakeOpener, FakeTester are all cfg(test) inline. The test-helpers feature in Cargo.toml:51 is empty (pure compile-gate). No public test-only types leak into non-test builds.

issues.title: FakeTransport never simulates ProbeError variants in CDN tests
issues.description: Every CDN-mode test uses only ok() or empty FakeTransport (implicit Refused). No test injects ProbeError::Timeout, ProbeError::TlsHandshake, or ProbeError::ConnectionRefused into a CDN scan path. The probe loop's error-to-fail_reason mapping is untested at the CDN level. Add 2-3 tests scripting failure variants to exercise that path.

issues.title: TunnelOpener::open() returning Err during speed testing is untested
issues.description: FakeOpener always returns Ok. The error path in measure_through_tunnel (which records the error on the verdict via apply_speed_result) is never exercised. Add one test where FakeOpener.open() returns Err and verify the verdict records the sanitized error.

issues.title: FakeTunnelProbe never produces passed=true with latency_ms=None
issues.description: Real tunnel probes can produce a passing result without a measured latency. The code handles this but no test covers this edge case. Add a test with a colo-only result to exercise it.

issues.title: FakeSub duplicated across configs.rs:1096 and engine/test_helpers.rs
issues.description: Two independent FakeSub implementations exist. Both wrap a string and return it from fetch(). Consider consolidating, though both are trivial and unlikely to diverge.

issues.title: No Arc-drop or mid-flight transport failure simulation
issues.description: All mocks succeed on construction. No test simulates Arc<dyn Transport> being dropped mid-scan. Mutex poisoning is tested, but transport-level mid-flight failures beyond the scripted set are not.

issues.title: Mock infrastructure overall is well-architected
issues.description: All six injectable dependencies have test doubles. The milestone stress test is an 8-thread correctness verification with uniqueness and monotonicity checks. Cancel-race tests use real barriers. Quality-gated stop exercises the full multi-pass scan loop. Sort correctness is covered by three dedicated tests. The primary gap is CDN error-path coverage at the transport level.

issues.issue: Silent early-return on non-matching data dir. If `data_dir.starts_with(&tmp)` is false, the test prints a message and returns Ok(()) -- it passes without running any assertions. This masks regressions in CF_SCANNER_DATA_DIR handling.
issues.fix: Either panic with a clear error, or gate the test with #[cfg] so it is properly ignored in CI environments where the path cannot be redirected.

issues.issue: Returns early without any assertion when CFSCANNER_SUB_URL is unset. Combined with #[ignore], this means the test effectively never runs in CI and the early-return makes it silently succeed when it does run without the env var.
issues.fix: Remove the early return. If the test is #[ignore], the env var check should panic with a clear skip message, not silently return Ok(().).

issues.issue: Uses .expect() which panics with a confusing message if the subscription fetch fails. The assertion only checks that specs is non-empty, not that the configs have expected fields.
issues.fix: Replace .expect() with .unwrap_or_else() that prints the URL, and add assertions on at least one spec's protocol and security fields.

issues.issue: The second scan run writes to JSON but does not verify the CSV from the first run was overwritten or left intact. The two export runs are independent, so a broken atomic-write could still pass the test.
issues.fix: Add an assertion after the second run that the CSV file still exists and its content matches the expected schema, or remove the CSV path if it's not the focus.

issues.issue: assert!(text.contains("scan")) is too weak -- it would pass if 'scan' appeared in any context (e.g., inside a URL or unrelated word).
issues.fix: Use assert!(text.contains("\n  scan ") || text.contains("\tscan ")) to check that 'scan' appears as a subcommand, not buried in prose.

issues.issue: Hardcodes the exact 14-column CSV header as a string literal. If a new column is added to the CSV output, this test breaks even though the behavior is correct.
issues.fix: Derive the expected header from the CSV column definitions (or count columns from the passing() helper's fields) rather than a literal string.

issues.issue: Uses `if geo.country.is_none() { return; }` -- silently passes when the mmdb is absent, which is the case on some CI runners.
issues.fix: Either embed a test fixture mmdb or mark this #[ignore] with a clear explanation, rather than silently passing.

issues.issue: Same silent-pass pattern as the v4 test above.
issues.fix: Same fix: #[ignore] or a dedicated test fixture.

issues.issue: Tests that decode_chunked(b"") returns an error, but does not verify the error message content. A future refactor that changes the error type would still pass.
issues.fix: Add an assertion on the error message or type: assert!(matches!(decode_chunked(b""), Err(e) if e.to_string().contains("empty")));

issues.issue: assert!(c.validate().is_err()) is too loose -- it would pass if the error was a completely wrong variant (e.g., InvalidPort instead of InvalidCidr).
issues.fix: Use assert!(matches!(c.validate(), Err(ConfigError::InvalidCidr(_, _))) for each case, or at minimum check the error message contains 'CIDR'.

issues.issue: The '::1' case uses assert!(w.validate().is_err()) without checking the error variant. A wrong error type would pass.
issues.fix: Use assert!(matches!(w.validate(), Err(ConfigError::NonRoutableEndpoint(_)))) for the loopback case.

issues.issue: assert_eq!(summary.scanned, 8 * 256) is a count-only assertion. If the scan visits some hosts twice and skips others, the count could still match.
issues.fix: Collect all scanned IPs from results and assert that no duplicate (ip, port) pairs exist, or check that the set of scanned IPs has cardinality 8 * 256.

issues.issue: Heavy use of .unwrap() in TLS server setup (e.g., rcgen::generate_simple_self_signed(...).unwrap(), tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(...).await.unwrap()). If setup fails, the panic message is a bare 'called Result::unwrap() on an Err' with no context about which test or what failed.
issues.fix: Replace key setup unwraps with .expect("descriptive message") so failures are diagnosable, e.g., .expect("test TLS cert generation").

issues.issue: No test exercises send_http / get_via_socks from multiple tasks concurrently against the same socks proxy. A race in the SOCKS state machine would go undetected.
issues.fix: Add a test that spawns N concurrent get_via_socks calls against a single fake_socks_server and asserts all complete successfully.

issues.issue: Store is Arc<Mutex<Vec<Verdict>>> but there is no test that pushes verdicts from multiple threads concurrently and then checks consistency.
issues.fix: Add a test that spawns 8 threads each pushing 1000 verdicts, then asserts results().len() == 8000 and results() is sorted.

issues.issue: No test for excluding a /32 (single-host) from a /128 pool, or excluding a prefix equal to the pool prefix (full removal).
issues.fix: Add tests: (1) pool of /128 excluding /128 = empty, (2) pool of /128 excluding non-overlapping /128 = unchanged, (3) pool of /64 excluding /32 = error or empty.

issues.issue: No test for spawn_with_retry when the closure returns an error on every attempt (always fails). Only 3-failure is tested.
issues.fix: Add a test where the closure always fails, and assert the error propagates after exactly MAX_RETRIES attempts with the final error message.

issues.test: Missing: src/configs.rs parse_uri with deeply malformed base64 in vmess
issues.issue: The vmess parser uses base64 decode but there is no test for vmess URIs with valid base64 that decodes to JSON with missing required fields (e.g., no 'add' key).
issues.fix: Add tests: vmess with base64 that decodes to {}, vmess with base64 that decodes to {"v":"2"} (missing add/port/id), vmess with base64 that decodes to valid JSON but with wrong 'v' value.

issues.issue: No test for what happens when the subscription fetch fails during phase-2 (network error, timeout). The FakeSub always succeeds.
issues.fix: Add a test with a FakeSub that returns Err, and assert the scan completes with phase2_passed=false and a meaningful fail_reason.

issues.test: Missing: src/export.rs export with IPv6-only results to all bundle formats
issues.issue: Only tests IPv6 rejection for the 'raw' bundle format. Other formats (singbox, clash, sharelinks) are not tested with IPv6-only input.
issues.fix: Add IPv6-only assertions for singbox, clash, and sharelinks bundle formats.
